messages.text: Pool at 8? Or are you buried under church food, Marisol pickup, and those paint class papers again?
Buried. I was up at 2:30 writing columns for bills, work calls, and who needs rides. Then I wiped the kitchen counters twice.
Come swim and leave one thing off the list. Also keep that number from your doctor card handy, even if you just ask questions.
I put it in my purse. Not calling today, but I do want to know what that first visit is like if these nights keep happening.
I found the little cooking place in Oaxaca with the blue doorway. Same one you showed me from your old photos.
Send it, but don't let me click too much tonight. I already moved $40 into the small envelope after the emergency transfer.
Did you save the flyer from the paint-safety table at church? The one with the Saturday hours.
Yes. It asks for my old school dates too, so I need to dig in the file box before I sign up.
Good. Blue doorway can wait. Also found a photo set of those wild tile benches in Barcelona you liked.
Bring it after swim if you want. I can help you read the tiny print before potluck prep starts.
Those benches and the crooked-looking church still make me stare. For now I am just saving pictures.
Good. I also circled the evening class about estimates and receipts. That one looks useful.
If the hallway outlets are loose, I can stop by after my job. Don't cover those plates until I check them.
Good. I already pulled the plates, patched the two dents by the switch, and taped the baseboards. Plastic is down from the door to the stairs.
You still keep the floor cleaner than most crews I see.
That's how Mr. Alvarez taught me back when you were little: prep first, then no one has to scrub after me.
Ma, Sunday I can bring chicken from the grill place if that works.
I can look at that garage subpanel photo after dinner. Tell Raul not to touch the conduit until I see it.
Good. I had him and Leo stay on masking and baseboards today. The hallway took longer because Leo kept loading the brush too heavy.
That works. I am skipping the fried tray this time and keeping my little cuff notebook on the counter.
New guy?
Ok. Text me the two numbers before dinner so I know you did it.
Yes. Reminds me of when I was learning with Marisol in kindergarten and Daniel still in diapers. Slow hands, but he listens.
I will. Also no chips from the gas station, bring fruit if you stop.
Ma, the city meeting link you sent has a part about patrol stops near job sites. You still want me to read it before Sunday?
Yes, mijo. I want to understand it better. I like when someone comes fast if there is trouble, but I don't like how the vans full of Spanish-speaking workers get watched.
They also list dash video rules and how complaints get reviewed. That's the part I noticed.
Good. Bring it Sunday. Roberto said the background forms for the school volunteer thing were simple, all the boxes we expected were blank.
Mom, I sent you the LA County page again. It has the spring schedule by age and location.
Thank you. I am going to compare it with the note from Dr. Nguyen before I book anything.
Good. The school nurse said the pharmacy list changes fast, so check the county one before you drive over.
I will. Walgreens on Seal Beach Blvd still has openings Wednesday morning.
Kids are already asking what you're making Sunday. Mia said the green sauce from last time.
Tell her I'll pull a few chilies and cilantro from the pots if they behave. Beans can start soaking Saturday.
Perfect. Do you want me to bring anything besides tortillas?
Maybe limes. Roberto finished that hallway corner too, such a straight tape line I keep walking by to look at it.
Mom, I put the kids' science night pictures in the album. Can you see them on the blue app?
Yes, I saw them. I also saw the parish fish fry notice right under it and saved the flyer.
Good. Before you get lost scrolling, Daniel tagged you on that purple-and-gold halftime clip again.
I tapped the heart and got out. Then I sent myself that green cabinet color from the camera app.
I looked at the kitchen. We still have two cans of soup, half a bag of rice, and tortillas.
Marisol said her school meeting may run late Friday. Booster seat is back in the garage.
Good. I can add eggs and salsa tonight so we do not touch the grocery card yet.
Thank you. I wanted to check with you before I tell her yes for Friday night.
Friday is okay. Keep Saturday morning simple and ask Marisol to pack the pajamas this time.
Fine with me. I paid Edison and the car insurance, so March sheet is already at 2,140 without food.
Then keep the receipt pile together. I want to see where we land before Friday.
I will. If it gets too crowded, I may call Teresa before I answer about the church kitchen too.
Did the Bellflower apartment guy give you a regular check or another 1099 one?
1099 again. Two bedrooms and trim, same as the last three places.
Then keep the sick hours at the school job for your shoulder. Don't burn them on those little side jobs.
I know. I still have 13.5 hours on the stub, and the clinic card renews through that account next month.
Do you remember if the old school forms used Angie or Angel? I found one from Santa Ana with both.
At home it was always Angelita when Mom was calling us in. The teachers wrote Angel on everything.
Same house, two names. I can still hear Dad saying apurate before the morning bell.
Bring that form Sunday if it has the 9/14 line. Marisol is helping me compare the dates.
If you make the rice Sunday, don't make a giant tray. Save your shoulder.
I know. Just enough for Roberto, you, and plates for Marisol if she comes up from Long Beach.
And Daniel? He said last time he was coming after a job, all dusty.
Depends where they send him that day. I told him I can keep his plate in the warm oven.
Ma, I looked at that county packet. The wording on Prop 3 is doing too much.
That's the one I circled. Page 27 says one thing and the short summary sounds different.
Send me a photo of the page after dinner. I'll read the fine print.
Okay. I also saved the church handout from Sunday, the part about listening before reacting.
Tia Lety asked what to set aside for you Saturday. Regular agua fresca, right?
Yes, thank you. Maybe one small glass for the birthday toast, then back to agua.
Got it. Also I told the cousins you and the kids are staying inside, not by the backyard table with the trays.
Perfect. And no dessert from that covered plate for me.
Mom, before you send that turmeric blood pressure thing to Tia, use the county clinic page I texted you last month.
Yes, I was waiting. The post made it sound too easy.
Same with that pan set from the video. I found the company site and reviews, but the page you showed me had no address.
Then I leave it. If it is not the same seller from the church fair, I am not putting my card there.
You done at Walgreens?
Yes. The pharmacist said keep the little card with my wallet and drink extra water today.
Left arm again?
Right this time. I have the printout in my purse in case Dr. Nguyen asks at my checkup.
The Civic estimate came in at $398. I told them we would call back tomorrow.
We can use the house cushion if we have to, but I want to see Friday's deposit first.
Okay. Also that office on Anaheim St left another reminder.
I know. I am going to ask them what part has to be paid up front before I pick a date.
I found the old notebook in my Anaheim garage. Your handwriting is all over the pages with Dr. Salazar times and what we packed for her lunches.
Keep it for now. I want to show Luis when he drives in from Riverside for the March 15 dinner.
I remember you doing the Tuesday rides and me doing the chopped vegetables and pillbox labels.
We were a team. I still make rice the way she could actually finish it.
How is your shoulder after all that folding at church?
Prima Lupe found another box from Tia Licha. Baptism paper says Jalisco on one side and a town near Oaxaca on the other.
Stiff, but I ate first and only took the two little brown tablets after dinner. Now I have manzanilla steeping.
Did you mark that sample ballot yet or are you still circling every school and clinic question like homework?
Save it for me. Those forms at the clinic never have a box that fits all that.
For Marisol's family page, was it the Santa Ana place with the avocado tree or the apartment before that?
Avocado tree. You and I were in the back room, Luis had that squeaky top bunk, and our cousin took the sofa for a while.
I marked the school bond maybe, the clinic funding yes, and I wrote a question mark by the housing one until I read the cost page.
Good. Put the arnica on before bed too, and don't keep reaching for that bottle every time it nags.
Right. Dad leaving with the mower before we woke up, Mom ironing those white uniforms late.
Yes, just tonight. Roberto already rubbed some on my shoulder and I am resting.
Good. The loud flyer in my mailbox had three promises and no math.
Exactly. Mom always said we were a whole mix before anyone tried to put it on one line.
Yes, and both of them still asking if we locked the screen door like we were kids.
That one went straight in the recycling. I want help for rent and wages, but I still need to see how they plan to pay for it.
I want Marisol to scan it before the papers fade.
Pool at 7:30 tomorrow? I saved us the slow lane before the loud class starts.
Yes, slow lane is perfect. My hands were fussy after chopping onions for church, so I am keeping the pace easy.
Bring the blue hand paddles only if they feel good. We can just do laps and then one small loop outside.
Deal. I will wear the cushioned shoes for the loop.
Do you still need my work lights for those stage panels tomorrow?
Yes, just the two tall ones. We are covering the old water stains before the Sunday crowd sees them.
I'll drop them by after the job in Garden Grove. Don't climb the ladder if Roberto isn't there.
I will stay on the low trim. Carmen already claimed the top corners.
I saved you a spot in lane 3 tomorrow if your shoulder behaves. Same benches by the pier at 6:10?
Yes. I will put my phone on the charger now and keep it in the little pouch until the sun comes up.
Good. And bring the green salsa recipe card for St. Anne after laps, not the whole binder.
Only the card. If you see me reaching for extra trays, give me that look.
Are you still hosting after Mass tomorrow, or should I bring the tray straight to your place?
Bring it here. Roberto already cleared the small table, and I only set out the extra chairs when everyone comes.
Good. Last time your front room in Seal Beach filled up fast.
I know. Once people leave, it goes right back to our quiet little setup.
Did you finish the last chapter before swim tomorrow?
Almost. I keep thinking the quiet husband is too obvious.
Ha. Save that for Elaine's table. You always spot the tiny clue before the rest of us.
I marked two pages, but no speeches from me this time.
For Saturday, I put you down for salsa and napkins, not the whole hot table.
I put you down for trays, not the whole kitchen. Say no if they ask for more.
Good. I can bring two trays if I prep Friday, but I am not staying late in the kitchen.
Good. I already chopped the chiles and I am leaving the rest for after the 6:30 swim.
That is plenty. Remember last October when the job ran past dinner and you still tried to carry the church list?
Stretch first. Then sit with your plants before you start stirring everything.
I remember. This time I will leave room in the day and let someone else handle the big pans.
That sounds right. I will bring the lighter salsa for after Mass.
Ma, do you still need me Sunday or did Marisol move dinner later?
Later. I moved it on my list after she sent the school thing. Also remind your dad I already sent the Toyota amount for March.
Got it. He was asking if the truck parts can wait.
They can wait. I want the cards cleared first, then we see what is left.
Pool opens at 7 Saturday. Bring the blue band; your left shoulder was tight last time.
I packed it already. Also leaving the soft black shoes in the car for after church prep.
Good. And take the folding stool if they put you on trays again.
I will. I told Rosa I can chop for one hour, then I switch with someone.
Ma, did that Belmont hallway lady pay the last piece yet?
Yes, the $520 came in. I put it with the other February checks before I touch any of it.
Good. And don't stack Saturday too. You already had five days on your board.
I know. This week is 36.5 if the Thursday trim doesn't run long.
Ma, can you answer quick? The front office phones start at 7:45 and I can't be late today.
I'm here. Do you need me for pickup or just breakfast money?
Pickup if the meeting runs past 3. Daniel won't be nearby unless his Garden Grove call finishes early.
Text me when you know. I'll keep my phone on.
Send me that clip with the chile roasting. Mine keeps burning on one side.
I saved it on the red app. It is the one where the lady turns them with tongs every minute, not the fork.
Good. Also bring that Celia one for cleanup after potluck, the one that gets everyone moving.
Already in the same queue with the Marc Anthony one Roberto likes after dinner.
I sent you the lighter mole one from the little video. Don't add the extra oil like she does.
I saved it with the basil planter picture. That app keeps showing me kitchen colors after I looked once.
Use it for ideas, not another project. Also the parish breakfast time changed on the group page.
I saw that after Teresa's birthday pictures. I clicked going, then closed it before the ball clips started.
For the potluck, are you doing the dark sauce or should I bring mine?
I'll do a smaller pot. I have tomatoes on the sill and enough oregano, but not enough sesame.
I have sesame. And don't make it too heavy, your shoulder will complain.
I know. I'll keep the radio on while it thickens, makes the stirring feel less like work.
I found the tissue flowers from last October in the pantry, but the orange ones are smashed.
Save the good ones. I can repaint the wooden arches before the next planning table.
Good, but only one arch. You promised me you would not take all three again.
One arch and the photo shelf trim. Hold me to it after the 9:30.
Ma, for the old-house paint jobs, ask if the class covers containment plastic and HEPA cleanup. That's what inspectors look for.
I wrote those words down. The form also wants dates for the classes I took before you and Marisol were little.
LBCC should still have something. Don't guess if the paperwork has a records box.
I'll call tomorrow. Then I can finish the sign-up and look at the QuickBooks night option.
Ma, Roberto said you redid the whole pantry after dinner. Everything okay?
Too many tabs open in my head. Insurance bill, work schedule, church trays, your dad's car noise. The pantry was just there.
Send me the car sound tomorrow. And maybe don't add the church trays.
I crossed off two trays. I also found the little paper Dr. Rivera gave me, in case I need someone neutral to help me sort this out.
Mom, the airfare alert you forwarded has a 36-hour timer. You want me to check if it's real?
Just check the fine print. I am not buying anything while the car repair and Roberto's account review are still open.
It is legit but the good dates are tight. The Barcelona one lands near that big church with the towers.
Save it in the folder with the Oaxaca notes. Looking is enough this week.
Do you want me to bring anything Sunday, Mom? The kids asked for chicken again.
No chicken this week. I have beans soaking and enough tortillas. Maybe you bring oranges if they are on sale.
Okay. I saw your envelope photo from Dad. Are you trying to keep groceries under 520 for March?
Yes, because the house lines already ate a lot. We will do simple plates and nobody will suffer.
Mom, after pickup I can explain the school board section. The wording is not friendly.
Gracias. I put tabs on the local pages and the two state ones I don't understand.
Bring the booklet Sunday. Also, did the $20 envelope get to Sister Elena?
Yes, I handed it to her after the hall meeting. I stayed for the small group and came home before the downtown crowd got loud.
I put the folding table in your truck. You said you needed space for the two helpers to lay out brushes.
Thanks. I want them doing the doors the same way before I leave for the walkthrough at 2.
Don't carry all the ladders yourself. And keep the papers from the walkthrough in the blue folder.
I know. The blue folder is the one with the license notes and the numbers we talked about after dinner.
The passport place wants your parents' towns written exactly. Do you want me to leave those blanks for you?
Yes, leave them. Mine is easy with California, but theirs I want to spell right from the old papers.
I put the envelope with your Santa Ana copy on the kitchen table.
Thanks. I will fill it after work before Marisol comes by.
I can meet you by the pier after the pharmacy. Want the flat path or the sand side?
Flat path, please. Stairs were not my friend this morning.
Okay. I will park near the benches so you do not have to climb back up.
Thank you. A steady walk will loosen me up before dinner.
Did Roberto find the old paperwork for Marisol's field trip clearance?
Yes. Mine and his were easy. Marisol said Daniel's contractor badge was the same, nothing to explain.
Good. Then don't let that city meeting make you carry everyone else's stress.
I know. I just keep thinking of the men outside Home Depot getting asked questions while the real problem on the corner needs a van with a nurse and a bed somewhere.
Roberto says I should not take the extra Saturday kitchen shift. Marisol said the same, but tell me straight before I answer.
Then answer no. You already have enough on your plate.
Are the little ones still coming Sunday or did Marisol change it again?
Just lunch this week. She is taking them back before bath time.
Ma, for the Costa Mesa condo, ask if they want a COI or just the invoice. Some small GCs skip half the paperwork.
They only asked for invoice, W-9, and photos when the cabinets are touched up.
Take a real break after. If the shoulder gets loud, use one of those hours from your other check.
I have a few saved. I also need Marisol to help me pick the cheaper plan before the portal closes.
Dad asked if I can look at the porch light Sunday. Still flickering?
Yes, but do not buy anything yet. Roberto and I are trying to keep repairs small until the big house payment clears.
I can check the wiring first. If it is just the fixture, I will tell you before you spend.
Thanks, mijo. It will only be us here after dinner, so no rush if you come later.
One of the guys at work said that speech downtown was all about blaming people who just got here.
That turns me off right away. My questions are wages, job safety, schools, and whether families can stay in their apartments.
Yeah, yelling about neighbors does not fix a paycheck.
Exactly. Talk to workers with respect and show the plan, then I will listen.
The school display asks for one line about each grandparent. Can I write that Grandpa got through sexto in Mexico?
Yes, about sixth. For Grandma, keep it simple too, around fifth or the lower grades there.
And the Santa Ana photo with you, Tia Teresa, Uncle Luis, and the cousin on the porch is okay?
Use that one. It shows the house better than the birthday picture.
Fog is thick by Electric Ave. Take the lit blocks until you meet your people.
I see Carmen's car already. We are starting by the library side, then cutting back to the water.
Text me when you get to the pool.
Here now. Carmen waited while I changed shoes.
You still at the Belmont place?
Finishing baseboards only. I moved the crown molding to Monday morning so I am not doing two tall walls in one afternoon.
Good. I will make soup and tortillas. No store run after.
Thank you. I want the work done right, but I am learning not to stack everything on one day.
You still reading? Light is on.
One more chapter. The narrator is hiding something, I can feel it.
Coffee will be ready early then.
Are you free to take Tia to the 24th appointment or should I ask Lili?
I can, but not before 2. I have the house payment set that morning and Marisol's pickup note right after.
You and your little notebook. Okay, 2 is better anyway.
Notebook keeps Roberto from asking twice. And it keeps me from paying the card people one day late.
For the church table, are you bringing the mole or the nopales salad? I am making room next to the Jalisco bread.
Mole. My aunt wrote the recipe with the chiles the old way, and Roberto already bought sesame seeds.
Good. Put your family's town names on the recipe card like last year. People liked seeing where each dish came from.
I'll write both sides, abuela's and grandpa's, so nobody argues with me.
Mom, did they send the numbers in writing? I can look after the kids' soccer game.
They emailed it. The first part is $420 before insurance answers, so I am not clicking anything yet.
Forward it to me. Maybe there is a cheaper slot or a plan.
I will. I just don't want to empty the cushion for something that can be arranged better.
I put the gray pair by the back door. The old ones are still wet from yesterday.
Thank you. I need the gray ones for the ladder room. Too much walking today.
Want me to move the paint boxes before I leave?
Yes, just the two heavy ones. I can do labels and take my first sit-down at 10.
You want me to rinse the sprayer parts in the garage sink or leave them?
Leave them soaking. I still need to wipe the ladder feet and fold the runners before dinner.
Your shoulder okay after all that rolling?
It'll complain, like it has since the old apartment jobs in the 90s. But the edges came out smooth.
Pool was quiet today. I am in the yard now before Roberto and I go to the church breakfast.
Stay there a few more minutes. Call me before you answer anyone about the extra signup sheet.
I will. I put soup on low too, so lunch is not another rush.
Good. We can talk on the way after you lock up.
For Tia's lunch, I made beans without the ham hock. Do not laugh, they still taste good.
Good, because Roberto keeps offering to bring carnitas and I am trying to be careful this month.
Bring your little machine if you are staying late. Last time you forgot and then worried about your evening numbers.
It is already in my bag with the notebook. I will bring salsa instead of the sweet bread.
For Sunday, Mike's bringing his balcony setup again. You want me to grab seats by the kitchen?
Yes please. Kitchen side is better, and tell him not to hand me anything from his little tin.
Done. I also picked up sparkling waters so nobody keeps refilling your glass.
Good. I only did the toast at Lety's and that was enough for the month.
Mom, did your knees calm down after swim yesterday?
A little. I skipped the bottle this morning and made ginger with cinnamon instead.
Okay. Eat breakfast before anything stronger, please. I can bring caldo after pickup if you want.
Breakfast first, yes. Caldo sounds perfect if it is not too much trouble.
Do you want me to put extra chairs out before Teresa gets here from Anaheim?
Yes, and leave one spot by the driveway for Luis. Riverside traffic may make him late.
I also set aside the low-sugar pan dulce recipe card you and Teresa used to make for your mom.
Thank you. She liked that one after morning appointments, especially with the cinnamon tea.
Did you order that knee wrap from the video?
No. The comments were all the same words and I could not find a real phone number.
Good. Also Teresa sent me the onion cure thing. You answering her?
After I read the hospital page. I am not sending it around just because cousin Lety liked it.
The kids left their plates. Want me to wash or put on your loud kitchen songs first?
Put the horn-and-piano list from the TV app. The one we used after Marisol's birthday.
Same one Daniel tried to dance to?
Yes. After that I need the short roller clip again before I touch up the hallway trim tomorrow.
Did Roberto make you write down the tax pile yet, or are you hiding receipts in the prayer book again?
Very funny. I wrote it down: February total 3400, and I moved the set-aside before groceries.
Good. Also leave Friday night alone if you have another 7-hour day.
Friday is 7, Thursday is 8, and Wednesday might be 6 if Mrs. Lin chooses the lighter color.
Did you ever ask about that second spring one, or are you waiting?
I called Dr. Nguyen's office. They said my March 4 record is enough for now unless the county changes the age chart.
Good, because the ladies after Mass all had different stories.
That is why I wanted the office to check it. I am not going by hallway talk.
I found that photo of you in the white overalls holding Daniel on your hip. Was that the same apartment complex job?
Yes, the one by Cherry Ave. I would practice trim after you two fell asleep because I wanted my corners clean.
That explains why you notice every crooked line in my house now.
Now I notice Leo's too. Tomorrow he gets the closet walls before I let him near the front room.
Found your Wilson folder in the garage cabinet. Also one envelope from LBCC.
Thank you. Leave both on the kitchen table with the EPA printout.
The Saturday class says bring calculator and mask. You still going after your job?
Yes. I want the paint rules first, then the money side class after Easter.
Are you awake? I got up thinking about the March Visa and Monday's work order list.
I am now. Put the pen down, hermana. You do this when everyone hands you one more thing.
I already made a page: bills, Roberto's appointment, Marisol's pickup, potluck, class reading. Then I started mopping.
Tomorrow call the number on that card, even just to ask how it works. You don't have to keep using me and Roberto as the whole bench.
After swim I'm going to that church table about the bus stop campers. You coming or resting your shoulder?
I will come for a little while. I want to sign the card asking for outreach workers before more hard stops.
Good. And don't argue with that man who says badges fix everything.
I won't. I know they can help. I just want cameras on, calmer questions, and another option when someone is sleeping under a blanket.
Mom, for the contractor form, do you want the name accent marks how Grandpa wrote them or how the DMV has them?
Use DMV for the form. At home we can write it the way Grandpa did.
Got it. Also Marisol said your September dinner should be Sunday the 13th or Monday the 14th?
Monday is the real day, but Sunday may be easier for everyone.
Ma, don't plug the patio lights into that old strip. I'll bring a safer one.
Thank you. Are you coming from Garden Grove or straight from the site?
Garden Grove first. Marisol said she may beat me there if the office clears out on time.
Good. I won't start dinner until both of you text me.
I can stop by after work Sunday. Want me to grab charcoal or anything?
Charcoal yes. Your dad wants the pork outside, and I still need to grind the red chilies.
Got it. The wall by the side door looks clean now btw.
That little edge came out nice. I'll put the yellow blooms there so people see it when they come in.
Ma did you see the clip I sent? Blue hats finally got decent pitching tonight.
I saw it between Aunt Teresa's comments on the birthday pictures. I gave it a like for you.
You always find those before I text you. Purple-and-gold page posted the injury update too.
It came up after the neighborhood pothole post. I saved the rosemary planter idea and put the phone down.
I left the mailer on the table. The one with the hard-hat photo.
I saw it. He says he is for working people, but the small print says cut the clinic grants and delay school repairs.
Then why use the hard hat?
That is what bothers me. Do not pose with workers and then make their kids' classrooms and doctor visits harder.
You still coming tomorrow or are you buried in papers again?
Coming. I just finished adding Feb stubs, 3,850 and 2,950, and sorting March receipts.
Bring the calculator if you want. I made rice, but not enough for your whole crew.
No worries. I can bring beans and a stack of tortillas from home.
Swim at 9? I am bringing jicama and lime, not the crunchy bag from last week.
Yes. I did my cuff numbers already, so I can meet by the benches.
Good. After laps we can trade that lighter mole recipe, the one without frying the sauce first.
Perfect. I still want it to taste like ours, just easier on me.
Pool at 9:15? I still have your notes from the parish room.
Yes. Bring them if you can. The speaker's story stayed with me more than the signs outside.
I liked that you sat and asked questions. That fits you better than standing all afternoon.
After swimming I need to finish the sample pages before Sunday dinner, so Daniel and Marisol can help with the hard parts.
After swim, Rosa's nephew invited everyone to his patio. Loud music, little papers, fancy cans, the whole thing.
Then let's do soup by the front window instead. My towel and lungs don't need that patio.
Good. I will order caldo and lime water for us.
Perfect. If they bring the sweet tray around, wave it past me too.
Found an old metal lunch pail in the garage. Roberto says it might be Grandpa's.
Probably. He used to pack tortillas in that before going to yards and then later fixing things at the apartments.
There are two laundry tags inside too. One has Grandma's handwriting.
Save them for me. She marked everything, even after a long day with linens and rooms.
They are asking if the blue blankets are still in your hall closet for tonight.
They are washed. I checked with your dad already and he said one night is fine.
Thank you. I will drop them at 4 and pick them up after Mass tomorrow.
Kids are helping you wipe counters today, right? Tell them no spraying each other.
They are folding towels first. I put on the same Saturday songs Grandma used when Teresa and I had the bedroom window open.
The school office wall by the copier has that shiny patch again. Can you look at it after pickup Monday?
The dramatic ones with all the crying? Mateo calls those movie songs.
Good. If the garage leak gets worse, I may call Teresa before I promise anything else this weekend.
Yes. Send me a photo in daylight and one with the hallway light. I can bring the fan deck and make a small test spot behind the file cabinet.
Yes, and later I promised them the fast dinner list if they finish before the arroz video ends.
I'll ask the custodian to move the boxes. Please don't let them rush you like last time.
I won't. If the wall is dusty, I need time to wash it, fill the nail holes, and cover the carpet strip before anyone walks through.
Did the school office form ask that question again for the grandkids?
Yes. Marisol called because none of the choices say Jalisco, Oaxaca, the old family stories, and being born here.
Just write the note in the margin like you always do.
I did. One little square is not enough for our family.
Did you ever call that place back, or are you still keeping the paper on the fridge?
Still on the fridge. I wrote down May 6 as the earliest that does not squeeze April.
You and your lists. At least put the number in your phone so it does not disappear under coupons.
Already did. I also marked how much we need to leave untouched after the car bill.
The swim ladies are all talking about that patch for shoulder pain. One lady posted a link.
I saw it. I want the name of the store first, not just a pretty picture and a discount clock.
And the part about it replacing therapy sounds big.
Send me the box label if anyone buys it. I will look it up before I mention it at potluck.
Ma, I left the ladder in the garage. Don't move it by yourself.
I won't. My wrist complained after the pantry shelves, so I did the cream and hot tea first.
Good. If you use the tablets, don't mix a bunch of them just to finish chores.
No, mijo. One round after food only if I really need it. The tea is enough right now.
Luis texted me a photo from Riverside of that blue cooler. Same one we used for the little containers.
